entries.text: For H.E.R.B.I.E. in The Fantastic Four: First Steps, which could sound like neither Pixar nor Star Wars, Collins sent a batch of eight versions, some from his own voice, some pure synthesis. The one chosen was built on the idea of a battle droid impersonating WALL-E, using some of his Chopper techniques.

source.title: Skywalker Sound with Matthew Wood & David W Collins - Hosted by Carly King | @RebelScumCon 2025

entries.text: For Woman of the Hour's parking-lot scene, Solis's team thinned everything out and kept the production footsteps: great shoes on a slightly wet floor gave a gritty heel-toe. The level of Rodney's muttered threat was argued over a single dB, so the audience is never quite sure what he said.

source.title: The Sound of Woman of the Hour with Director Anna Kendrick

entries.text: Farmer has had his best luck on monitors that were underpowered or not the flattest, because they make him work harder. On flattering speakers like Mackie HR824s he stopped working on a sound too soon, since it already sounded good in his room, and it fell apart on the mix stage.

source.title: Sound Design and Re-Recording Mixing with David Farmer and Marc Fishman

entries.text: Hiland on The Midnight Sky's sinking-shelter sequence: snowmobile and ice cracking aren't string-friendly, so Todd Beckett's panning in Atmos, choosing where each effect plays in the room as well as which plays, is what left space for the score to get through.

source.title: The Midnight Sky - Mix Presents Award Season 2021

entries.text: For the ambience inside the mind in Inside Out, Klyce put microphones in sand and recorded crabs moving through it: a strange sound with movement and character that never sticks out.

source.title: The Sound of Inside Out

entries.text: On Parenthood, where storylines often have a band starting up or stopping mid-scene, Allen records the music live on set rather than relying on playback: a multitrack session through a Tascam DM-3200 with extra preamps, the room mic'd rock-and-roll style, so editors cut between angles with consistent live sound.

source.title: SoundWorks Collection: Production Sound Mixer Nicholas Allen

entries.text: To stop The Falcon and the Winter Soldier's hand-to-hand fights becoming a repetitive string of impacts, Patrick gave every hit its own sound and laid cloth layers over everything for the movement between blows. Without that Foley glue, she found, punches read as just a sound effect.

source.title: The Sound for The Falcon and The Winter Soldier - Mix Sessions

entries.text: Starting The Batman while the Warner Bros. lot was nearly empty during the pandemic, Files's crew recorded guerrilla effects around it: stomping on the catwalks, and Batman's footsteps echoing in a cavernous, unfinished concrete bunker beneath a new building.

source.title: Mix Magazine Sound for Film & TV 2022 - Sound Changes w/Will Files, Craig Henighan and Julian Slater

entries.text: On Judas and the Black Messiah, Lievsay mixed Fred Hampton's church rally, the film's hardest scene, first. His rule: always start a film with the hardest thing, because once that works and people are happy, the rest of the mix turns the corner.

source.title: Judas and the Black Messiah - Mix Presents Award Season 2021

entries.text: On David Fincher's films since Zodiac, Klyce mixes the music himself. Holding the music faders, he studies each layer Reznor and Ross deliver against picture, and finds that is the best way to make his sound design work with the score rather than favouring his own effects.

source.title: The Music in Sound with Ren Klyce

entries.text: For the baseline-test interrogator in Blade Runner 2049, Bartlett put the voice's direct signal in the Atmos overheads, with its reverb spread everywhere, so the voice sits on top of K and feels oppressive and claustrophobic. He finds sparse scenes show off Atmos more than dense action does.

source.title: Oscar Podcast - Blade Runner 2049 - Atmos

entries.text: On the Star Wars films, Wood's team cuts complete sound effects coverage under every scene, even where music is temped wall to wall, because the mix may try a section without music. Acord and his editors have to have all that material in place.

source.title: Conversations With Sound Artists: Star Wars | Podcast | Dolby

entries.text: Baby Yoda's vocals in The Mandalorian are partly Acord's own human voice, with recordings of a bat-eared fox and a kinkajou mixed in: a little bit of everything.

source.title: Conversations With Sound Artists: Star Wars | Podcast | Dolby

entries.text: When Mary enters the Backrooms, the rumbly, almost horse-like heartbeat is actually score. Battaglia, who wants music and sound design to merge rather than just dance together, gave that cue sound-effect treatment in the mix so the two act as one element.

source.title: The Sound of Backrooms

entries.text: Backrooms is found footage with no music and little beyond buzzing lights, so Battaglia emphasised the Foley of the person holding the camera. Leaning on the operator's movement keeps it from feeling like a floating camera and keeps the audience in a visceral, diegetic experience.

source.title: The Sound of Backrooms

entries.text: In Sound of Metal, the opening morning in Ruben's Airstream is mixed close and detailed, with the grinder right in your ear and single coffee drops. Becker describes the next day as a mirror: the same shots return, totally muffled, after Ruben loses his hearing.

source.title: The Sound of Metal - Mix Presents Award Season 2021

entries.text: When Ken first sees Barbie in Toy Story 3 he freezes and the song begins in mono; Semanick spreads it around the room as the camera zooms in, so it wraps around the audience as if everything else has gone for Ken.

source.title: The Sound of “Toy Story 3”

entries.text: For General Grievous in Revenge of the Sith, Wood's team set one voice process before casting, a little ring modulation and some distortion, pitching each auditioning actor up or down as needed, so every candidate Lucas heard went through the same chain.

source.title: Inside the Sound of Star Wars: A Conversation with Ben Burtt & Matthew Wood

entries.text: For the Mustafar lava duel in Revenge of the Sith, Burtt started from real volcano recordings a scientist made in Hawaii, sweetened the lava bursts with explosions, and added a Niagara Falls roar, EQ'd different ways for its liquid feel, while keeping the lightsaber fight articulate on top.

source.title: Inside the Sound of Star Wars: A Conversation with Ben Burtt & Matthew Wood

entries.text: Wood on the seismic charge in Attack of the Clones: after many effects were tried for the initial blast over ILM's reverse-style visual, Burtt suggested in the mix playing nothing at all there, so the first sound was removed and only the big explosion lands.

source.title: Matthew Wood & David W. Collins Talk Skywalker Sound, Voice Acting, Film Soundtracks, and more!

entries.text: Mixing F9's score from Brian Tyler's 60 to 80 stereo pairs, Taylor keeps only the drum kit fixed up front; everything else moves around the room in rhythm, horns and strings always spatially separated, so the music stays clear under busy effects without added reverb.

source.title: The Sound of F9: The Fast Saga

entries.text: For the Ferrix funeral procession in Andor's season 1 finale, Acord made the band sound different wherever the cut landed, shaped by distance and buildings, drawing closer until it filled the street, then stopping; the anvil striker earlier got the same treatment.

source.title: The Sound of Andor - Season 1 with David Acord, Margit Pfeiffer and John Gilroy

entries.text: For Vision and the twins breaking apart in WandaVision's finale, Foscato reused an earlier treatment of Vision straining against the Hex: two Dehumanizer presets, one glitchy, layered with the regular voices, so the dialogue broke up while the performances stayed intact.

source.title: The Sound for WandaVision - Mix Sessions

entries.text: For R5-D4's fear in The Mandalorian season 3, worked out with Favreau during the mix, the sound that won for the droid shaking was Collins's own: a couple of pairs of his kids' shoes knocking around in a dryer.

source.title: Behind the Sound of The Mandalorian (Season 3) & Obi-Wan Kenobi

entries.text: On TRON: Legacy, the light-up costumes put a whine on production dialogue that shifted pitch per actor. Whittle's team had the dialogue editors cut with the whine in, then sent the edits out for spectral noise removal, keeping the original edit on hand for the 15 to 20% it couldn't fix.

source.title: TRON: Legacy Sound Panel

entries.text: To make TRON: Legacy's discs sound dangerous, Boeddeker didn't layer in metal blades. He ran the disc tone through his resonator process, pitching in minute, very sharp frequencies that gave it an edge while keeping the pulse that let its Doppler read.

source.title: TRON: Legacy Sound Panel

entries.text: In The Bear's family-dinner blow-up, Giammaria had the fork throw covered three ways: clean production, Foley and an extreme designed version. Mapping the dynamics of throw, table flip and car crash, he dialed the throw back to mostly production, a little Foley and one small whip for air, so the table hit could land.

source.title: The Sound of The Bear

entries.text: In Scott Pilgrim vs. the World, Slater's team didn't accompany whip pans with generic whooshes. Each pan got a diegetic sound from its location instead: a cappuccino-machine whoosh in the coffee shop, a car passing when the scene is on the street.

source.title: SoundWorks Collection: The Sound of Scott Pilgrim vs. the World

entries.text: For the volumetric-capture simulation scenes in Demonic, Rossi built the ambiences in Atmos and down-mixed them: carefully picked backgrounds made to stutter, and birds played backwards that still read as birds. Heard alone the environment sounds otherworldly; under the sim it glued everything together.

source.title: The Sound of Demonic with Director Neill Blomkamp

entries.text: For the good-luck crystals in the animated feature Luck, Horner recorded a Christmas dog collar covered in tiny bells at a 100k sample rate so it could be pitched without artifacts. The sticky bad-luck crystals came from pill-shaped magnets, which give rhythm and texture instead of a flat click.

source.title: Mix Magazine Sound for Film & TV 2022 - Sound Design behind animated feature film “Luck”
